relevance_note: Cohort of HA20 patients with per-patient clinical data in Table 2 ('Detailed clinical history of all 16 patients included.'); in scope by HA20 diagnosis.
method_note: A Python script transcribed Table 2 (16 rows) into rows; I checked its output against the table. Labels follow the bare-number 'Patient number' column (Table 2 #1-#16); family_label_in_paper is the 'Family' cell (1-6). Table 2 codes cells as 1/0 with no legend; 1 was read as present (column counts match the text: mouth ulcers 16, genital ulcers 13, gut symptoms 13, colchicine 5). 0 is not defined as absent, so every 0 cell is 'not reported' (features and treatment). 'History of gut symptoms' and 'GI symptoms on collection day' were not mapped to any checklist item; 'History of colitis/gut ulcers' was mapped to 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation'; 'Liver disease' has no checklist item. No TNFAIP3 variant, sex, age, or diagnosis basis is given per patient (only 'mutational status' extracted from records), so no variants rows were made. Ethnicity is from the statement naming all 16 patients. The excluded 'auto‐antibodies specific to PSC' row for every patient comes from the Discussion group statement 'no patient displayed auto‐antibodies specific to PSC'; it does not exclude the broader checklist item 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)'. Unattributable subset results (5 MRI patients, histology of 1/3/1/4 patients, interferon signature in 5/5 tested, one patient on TNF-α blockers with sustained GI inflammation) were not assigned to anyone. Inconsistencies in the paper: Table 1 'Females 12 (71)' (12/16 is 75%) and controls '25 (78)' with n = 22; Table 1 abdominal pain on collection day 4 (25) vs 3 patients coded 1 for 'GI symptoms on collection day' in Table 2; 'Elevated liver enzymes were noted in 4 patients' vs 5 coded 1 for 'Liver disease' (possibly different measures). Three families were previously described (refs 11-13) but the paper does not say which patients, so source_reference_in_review is 'not reported'. No stacked cells.
